raw_text:
<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel app uses Laravel 12 ecosystem, Livewire 4, Flux 2, Pest 4, PHPUnit 12, Pint 1, Boost 2.

Activate relevant skills: `fluxui-development`, `livewire-development`, `pest-testing`, `tailwindcss-development`, `developing-with-fortify`.

Follow conventions; inspect siblings; use descriptive names, existing components and directories. Do not change dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

Use Boost MCP tools: `list-artisan-commands`, `get-absolute-url`, `tinker`, `database-query` (read-only), `database-schema` (before migrations/models), `browser-logs`. Always use `search-docs` before code changes for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem documentation; broad topics, multiple queries as useful, no package names.

If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. If Vite manifest errors occur, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Always use curly braces for control structures, including single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion (`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`). Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always declare explicit return types and parameter type hints. Prefer TitleCase Enum keys, PHPDoc blocks over inline comments, and useful array-shape definitions. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex.

Every change must be programmatically tested: write/update a test and run affected tests. Run minimum tests with `php artisan test --compact` plus filename/filter. Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues.

Laravel: Use `php artisan make:` with `--no-interaction` and correct `--options`; `php artisan make:class` for generic classes. Use typed Eloquent relationships, models/relationships and `Model::query()` over raw queries; avoid `DB::`; prevent N+1 with eager loading; query builder only for complex operations. New models should include useful factories/seeders; ask whether needed and use `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options. Use API Resources/versioning unless conventions differ. Always create Form Request classes with rules/custom messages, following siblings.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
